Implementation details of the mixed Markov random field in bgms.
Source: `src/models/mixed/mixed_mrf_model.h` and four `.cpp` files
(`mixed_mrf_model.cpp`, `mixed_mrf_gradient.cpp`,
`mixed_mrf_likelihoods.cpp`, `mixed_mrf_metropolis.cpp`).

## Block structure

The mixed MRF handles $p$ discrete and $q$ continuous variables. The
parameter space is organized into three interaction blocks plus
main effects:

| Block | Parameters | Size | Sampler |
|-------|-----------|------|---------|
| Main effects | Discrete thresholds + continuous means | $\text{thresholds} + q$ | NUTS |
| Discrete-discrete | $\mathbf{K}_{xx}$ (symmetric) | $p(p-1)/2$ | NUTS |
| Cross-type | $\mathbf{K}_{xy}$ | $p \times q$ | NUTS |
| Continuous-continuous | $\mathbf{K}_{yy}$ (precision) | $q(q+1)/2$ | Metropolis |

The continuous precision $\mathbf{K}_{yy}$ must remain positive
definite, so it is excluded from the NUTS block and updated by
element-wise Metropolis proposals with Cholesky rank-1 updates,
identical to the GGM strategy.

## Parameter vector layout

The model distinguishes three vector types:

### Active vector (`parameter_dimension()`)

Contains only the parameters that NUTS updates, excluding edges
set to zero by edge selection:

```
[ thresholds | K_xx (active) | means | K_xy (active) ]
```

The mass matrix and gradient are dimensioned to this vector.

### Full vector (`full_parameter_dimension()`)

Contains all NUTS-block parameters including inactive edges:

```
[ thresholds | K_xx (all) | means | K_xy (all) ]
```

Used for storage and initialization.

### Storage vector (`storage_dimension()`)

Adds the Metropolis-updated continuous precision to the full vector:

```
[ thresholds | K_xx (all) | means | K_xy (all) | K_yy (all) ]
```

This is what gets saved to `ChainResult::samples` at each iteration.

## Hybrid sampling strategy

Each MCMC iteration has two phases:

1. **NUTS phase** — Update the active parameter vector (thresholds,
   $\mathbf{K}_{xx}$, means, $\mathbf{K}_{xy}$) using one NUTS step.
   The `logp_and_gradient()` method computes the log-pseudoposterior
   and gradient for this block only.

2. **Metropolis phase** — Update the continuous precision elements
   ($\mathbf{K}_{yy}$) one at a time via
   `do_pairwise_continuous_metropolis_step()`. Each proposal uses a
   Gaussian perturbation with Robbins-Monro-tuned SD, followed by a
   Cholesky rank-1 update to maintain positive definiteness.

Edge indicator updates (when active) operate on all three interaction
blocks.

## Gradient computation

The gradient (`mixed_mrf_gradient.cpp`) is computed for the NUTS
block only. It involves:

1. **Discrete conditionals** — Category probabilities via
   [variable helpers](variable-helpers.qmd), contributing gradients
   for thresholds and $\mathbf{K}_{xx}$
2. **Cross-type terms** — Contributions from $\mathbf{K}_{xy}$ to
   both discrete and continuous conditional distributions
3. **Continuous means** — Gradient of the continuous-variable
   contribution to the pseudolikelihood

The log-prior gradient adds the Cauchy prior penalty on pairwise
interactions.

## Pseudolikelihood options

The `pseudolikelihood` argument controls the continuous-variable
likelihood:

- `"conditional"` (default) — Uses the conditional distribution of
  each continuous variable given the rest, consistent with the discrete
  pseudolikelihood
- `"marginal"` — Uses the marginal normal likelihood for the
  continuous block, which can be more efficient when $q$ is large

The choice affects both the log-posterior evaluation and the gradient
computation.

## Missing data

The mixed MRF tracks missing indices separately for discrete and
continuous variables (`missing_index_discrete`,
`missing_index_continuous`). During imputation:

- Missing discrete values are sampled from their full conditional
  categorical distributions
- Missing continuous values are sampled from their conditional normal
  distributions given the current precision matrix

## Output assembly

The R output builder (`build_output_mixed_mrf()` in `build_output.R`)
maps the flat storage vector back to the original variable ordering
using `fill_mixed_symmetric()`. This function places discrete-discrete,
continuous-continuous, and cross-type interactions into the correct
cells of the $(p+q) \times (p+q)$ output matrix, respecting the
original column order (which may interleave discrete and continuous
variables).
